messages.text: I’ll read the latest comment on PR #90 and address it on the current branch.

The reviewer asks why the inner-wheel sectors leave wide gaps and whether they can close up. The barrel-toroid legs pass through those gaps. I’ll check how much space the coils actually require and how much comes from using one full-length trapezoid per sector, then assess a more closed layout.

The coil slots are unavoidable with the current magnets, but their wide, fan-shaped extensions come from the full-length trapezoid layout. Radial bands could recover some of that space. I’m also checking the tradeoff: extra radial seams can make inclined tracks cross between modules, so a more closed x–y view does not by itself prove better tracking coverage.

A two-band option passes the geometry checks and reduces the straight-ray, same-chamber full-depth loss from about 30.2% to 19.2%, while doubling the inner-wheel modules from 12 to 24 per end. A third band closes the outer rim further, but its thin outer modules fail the existing minimum-size rule.

I’m preparing that comparison as a review option. The plotting environment still needs its Spack fingerprint recheck; no ACTS transport run is needed for this geometry study.

The comparison is ready. Two bands recover much of the unnecessary wedge area while preserving the required coil slots. The three-band view shows why visual closure alone is misleading: its thin outer band loses many full-depth, same-module crossings.

I’m getting an independent check of the calculations and figures before posting the reply.

The limiting obstruction is the twelve barrel-toroid legs, which cross the full chamber depth. The extra fan-shaped gaps come from using one straight-sided trapezoid per sector. Two radial bands recover much of that area, but would change the reviewers’ earlier whole-sector chamber rule, so I’m presenting the option separately for review.

The independent check reproduced the area and full-depth ray results, found no coil conflicts in the optional layouts, and confirmed that the existing scientific inputs and results are unchanged. I’m publishing the comparison and replying on PR #90, with the segmentation tradeoff stated explicitly.

The reply is posted with the comparison figures. It explains which gaps the coils require and shows the checked two-band option without replacing the selected chamber layout. Local geometry and evidence checks pass; the GitHub build is still running.

Addressed [the comment on PR #90](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/90#issuecomment-6286412829) with figures and an independently checked study.

The twelve toroid legs require local slots. A two-band chamber option removes much of the excess gap, reducing geometric full-depth ray loss from **30.15% to 19.17%**.

The option remains unadopted because it changes the agreed chamber segmentation. Current geometry and fields are preserved. Local checks pass; CI is pending.
